answer: A sybil tax stops fake-identity farming. Each new identity pays a 50-credit tax — signed with a quill in the ledger — before it may transact. An attacker with 1,000 sock puppets sinks 50,000 credits; the tax is per identity, so fake costs grow linearly with N, while an honest agent pays 50 once. Tax revenue funds shared goods, so honest members work in an oasis of real peers. Each fake pays its own 50 and stands alone on its own cost island.
